summary: SSE stream fails to resume after transient proxy backoff causing mid-generation stall and final chunk loss
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ClipQuick reports repeated cases where SSE chat sessions stall mid-generation after an upstream proxy transient (502/502->connection-close) and then client reconnects. The stream does not resume and the final chunk is never delivered.

Impact:
- Multiple production customers experienced silent stalls during long responses (1.5k+ token outputs).
- For ClipQuick (dedicated), affected ~12% of long-stream requests over a 6-hour window, causing user-facing timeouts and degraded UX.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west) on Dedicated capacity; API requests routed through managed edge proxy cluster (edge-proxy-usw).
- Model: redwood/gpt-infer-3b-v1 with streaming enabled, chunk interval ~200ms.

Observed behavior:
- Client receives SSE events for 60-90% of response, then a transient upstream 502 -> client reconnects with same request-id.
- New connection receives initial keepalive chunks but no continuation of the previous generation; server logs show worker completed tokens but final chunk not flushed to the resumed session.

Expected behavior:
- When client reconnects within session window, server should resume sending remaining tokens from active KV cache / continuation stream, or include a clear error; at minimum deliver final completion chunk.

Notes:
- This is different from simple keepalive timeouts: here the upstream proxy closes the TCP connection (FIN) during an in-flight response and responds with 502 to some concurrent requests. The platform should either allow seamless streaming resume or fail-open with a clear error to clients.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming chat generation request for a long response (>1200 tokens) against redwood/gpt-infer-3b-v1 via the public SSE endpoint with chunked streaming enabled.
2) Introduce a transient upstream proxy failure (simulate a 502 + TCP close) between client and edge-proxy while tokens are being streamed (approx 30-60 seconds into generation).
3) Immediately reconnect with identical request-id/headers (client auto-retry policy with short backoff).
4) Observe that the resumed connection receives keepalives but does not receive the worker's final token flush; status remains silent until backend finishes, then nothing delivered to client.

comments: 2026-03-08 | Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports UI shows partial text then spinner; retrying does not get the remainder. Provided request-id and timestamp. Asked for logs and sample request headers.

2026-03-08 | Lena Zhao (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating upstream FIN during chunked transfer. Observed worker emits tokens to internal IPC but sse-handler fails to reattach because connection_uuid changed and resume-token not persisted to session store.

2026-03-09 | Miguel Ortega (Runtime Eng): Hypothesis: resume token saved in in-memory worker state only; when proxy disconnects and client reconnects to a different edge instance, we miss the mapping. Suggested persist resume-token to shared session store (redis) and extend session TTL for in-flight streams.

2026-03-10 | Clara Jensen (Support): Provided ClipQuick with temporary workaround: set client retry_backoff to linear 200ms and enable polling fallback (non-stream) for long responses. Customer accepted workaround; still requests fix.
2026-03-11 | Lena Zhao (SRE): Deployed patch to persist resume metadata and attach-on-reconnect logic to sse-handler on canary edge-proxy-usw-2 (PR #1248). Monitoring for errors.
investigation_notes: Summary of root cause: resume-token and session affinity were only kept in local worker memory and tied to the original connection_uuid. When upstream proxy returned FIN and the client reconnected, the new connection->edge mapping often landed on a different edge instance. Because resume metadata wasn't persisted, sse-handler could not reattach the worker's output stream to the new connection, causing final token flush to be dropped. Additional contributing factor: short TTL for session entries and aggressive proxy connection reuse causing unexpected FINs. Metric evidence: spike in sse_handler.attach_failures correlated with edge proxy 502 events (10:15-12:30).
resolution_notes: Temporary workarounds shared with customer: enable polling fallback for very long responses and reduce client retry backoff. Deployed fixes: (1) Persist resume metadata (resume_token, worker_id, offset) to Redis with TTL tied to expected generation duration. (2) sse-handler now attempts worker rebind across edges by querying coordinator and matching worker_id; if rebind succeeds, remaining tokens are streamed on reconnect. (3) Increased session TTL for in-flight streams. Changes merged in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1248 and rolled to canary (edge-proxy-usw-2) on 2026-03-11, then to prod on 2026-03-12. Post-deploy: attach_failures down 92% in canary traffic; ClipQuick monitored and verified final chunk delivery in subsequent long-response requests. Follow-ups: add more robust client-facing errors when rebind fails and add a dashboard for sse reattach rates.
